_meta.gold_v2_note: EXPERIMENTAL CLONE. Original gold project is unchanged at frontend/project/gold/. This copy adds the 'normalized' entity, which implements threshold-ratio normalization as described in docs/ndc_measurement_framework.md Section 8.1. All other entities (synthetic, newmont, barrick, mining_co_a, mining_co_b) are preserved from the original without modification.

_normalization.formula: D = average(actual_i / threshold_i) for D primitives; C = average(actual_i / threshold_i) for C primitives
_normalization.scale_interpretation: 1.0 = at minimum viable threshold; > 1.0 = above threshold; < 1.0 = below threshold (non-viable)

normalized.label: Normalized (Threshold-Ratio)
normalized.description: Experimental entity. D and C values derived from ratios of actual physical and institutional values to documented minimum viable thresholds (docs/ndc_measurement_framework.md Section 8.1). Scale: 1.0 = at viability threshold. Sources: WGC 2023, LBMA Good Delivery Rules 2024, COMEX specs, Newmont 2024 SR, ICMM benchmarks.

synthetic.label: Synthetic Baseline

royal_mint.label: UK Royal Mint (Recycler)

normalized._note: Threshold-ratio normalized entity. D and C are averages of (actual/threshold) ratios for each phase's key primitives. Values in range 1.0-3.0. See _meta._normalization for full primitive definitions and sources.

0.notes: D primitives: exploration_cost_intensity (65/43=1.512), inferred_resource_fraction (42/28=1.500). C primitives: m_and_i_confidence (58/42=1.381), drill_coverage_density (50m/36m=1.389). Stressed zone in original flag-count model; normalized model shows Coherent — exploration phase is viable when grade is above cut-off.
0.balance_zone_note: 85.1% coherence. Exploration cost and resource uncertainty are above threshold but M+I confidence and drill density compensate.

1.notes: D primitives: energy_per_oz (95/73=1.301), regulatory_overhead (5/4=1.250), water_intensity (200/155=1.290). C primitives: recovery_rate (92/80=1.150), aisc_price_margin (1900/1350=1.407), water_recycling (22/15=1.467), site_diversity (8/6=1.333). C > D: mine extraction is contribution-led — AISC margin and site diversity drive system health.
1.balance_zone_note: 91.6% coherence. Extraction is well-balanced. Energy and water intensity are above minimum but offset by recovery rate and price margin.

2.notes: D primitives: energy_intensity (100/80=1.250), tailings_generation (97/95=1.021), reagent_consumption (0.5/0.38=1.316). C primitives: recovery_rate (85/75=1.133), water_recycling (75/60=1.250), concentrate_grade (100/75=1.333). C slightly > D: processing is contribution-led with excellent water recycling and grade output.
2.balance_zone_note: 93.3% coherence. The most mature phase in the chain — well-characterized D constraints and strong C metrics.

3.notes: D primitives: smelting_energy (50/35=1.429), impurity_content (25/18=1.389). C primitives: dore_purity (75/60=1.250), silver_recovery (70/55=1.273). D > C: smelting energy and impurity load exceed the contribution metrics. Normalized balance is lower than flag-count (89.3%) because thermal process energy is a genuine physical constraint.
3.balance_zone_note: 81.1% coherence. D-led phase: smelting energy and impurity removal constrain performance. Still coherent but close to stressed threshold.

4.notes: D primitives: lbma_fineness_spec (999.5/950=1.052), cert_steps (4/3=1.333), acid_precision (0.015/0.010=1.500). C primitives: refining_yield (99.9/99.0=1.009), lbma_compliance (100/95=1.053), throughput (10/6=1.667), brand_cert (100/85=1.176). D slightly > C: LBMA certification overhead adds real constraint load; throughput above minimum economic scale provides compensation.
4.balance_zone_note: 89.8% coherence. LBMA specification overhead is quantifiable as a D constraint, not just a flag. Throughput and compliance rates provide solid C.

5.notes: D primitives: cert_steps (3/2=1.500), assay_precision (0.010/0.005=2.000). C primitives: bar_acceptance (99.8/98.5=1.013), assay_turnaround (48h/24h=2.000), brand_recognition (15/8=1.875). D slightly > C: LBMA assay precision requirement is the tightest specification in the chain. The 2.000 ratio on assay precision is the highest D sub-score across all phases — physical constraint, not just structural.
5.balance_zone_note: 87.1% coherence. Assay precision adds the highest D ratio in the chain. Fast turnaround and large brand network provide strong C offset.

6.notes: D primitives: custody_opacity normalized (3/4*1+1=1.750), custody_fragmentation (15/5=3.000), transport_security_cost (15/8=1.875). C primitives: comex_vault_network (12/8=1.500), insurance_coverage (100/90=1.111), delivery_sla (5d/2d=2.500). BOTTLENECK. Custody fragmentation (3.000) is the highest single D sub-score in the chain. Opacity score of 3/4 adds further constraint. The gap is structural and governance-driven, not technology-driven.
6.balance_zone_note: 63.4% coherence — Stressed zone. Custody fragmentation and opacity are the dominant D drivers. Consistent with flag-count result (65.5%). Intervention: custody chain consolidation and opacity reduction.

7.notes: D primitives: regulatory_reporting (4/3.6=1.111), comex_delivery_overhead (1.111). C primitives: settlement_efficiency (99.9/99.0=1.009), market_transparency (95/85=1.118), delivery_acceptance (99.5/90=1.056 adjusted to 1.089). The exchange registration phase is closest to theoretical minimum in D and C — it is a highly standardized, rule-bound phase with little operational slack on either side.
7.balance_zone_note: 93.2% coherence. The most rule-standardized phase in the chain. D and C are both close to 1.0 (near minimum viable threshold on both sides).

8.notes: D primitives: feedstock_variability (cv 35/20=1.750), logistics_cost (22/14=1.571). C primitives: recovery_rate (85/70=1.214), supply_contribution (28/18=1.556), energy_reduction (60/35=1.714). D > C: feedstock variability is the primary constraint — recycled gold input grade ranges from 10 g/t (e-waste) to near-pure (dental, bar). Energy reduction advantage and 28% supply contribution are strong C factors but do not fully offset variability overhead.
8.balance_zone_note: 81.9% coherence. Just above Coherent threshold (80%). Feedstock variability is the primary D driver. Consistent with flag-count result (80.0%) — both methods identify this phase as marginal-coherent.

1.notes: High D-natural constraint (geology). High C from global production network. Source metrics: production_tonnes_year, economic_demonstrated_reserves_tonnes, economic_life_years, gdp_contribution_pct....
1.data_quality: Partial — mix of sector-level (Australia, 2003) and company-level (Newmont global, 2024)
1.scope_source: WGC Gold and Climate 2023; Foran et al. 2005 (13% direct/44% grid split applied to Phase 1)
1.scope_notes: Diesel haul trucks, blasting, dewatering (S1); ventilation, grinding mills (S2). S2 dominant at 25% clean energy mix.
1.water_source: Newmont/Barrick Sustainability Reports; ICMM Water Reporting Guidelines (benchmark 10-30%)
1.water_notes: Dust suppression 30-40%, ore washing 20-30%, equipment cooling 10-15%. Recycling mostly cooling water.
1.energy_source: WGC Gold and Climate 2023; Foran et al. 2005; Newmont 30% renewable target by 2030
1.energy_notes: Diesel 60-80% (haul trucks, excavators, drills); grid 10-30%; renewables 5-15% growing. Remote location limits grid access.

2.notes: 95% of ore becomes tailings (D-natural). Water recycling target: 75%.
2.data_quality: Partial — company-level (Newmont global, 2024) for environmental metrics; sector-level benchmarks available via Phase 1 Foran source
2.scope_source: WGC Gold and Climate 2023; Newmont 2024 Sustainability Report
2.scope_notes: Chemical heating, reagent production (S1); grinding mills, flotation, pumping — most electricity-intensive phase (S2).
2.water_notes: Cyanide leaching 40-50%, flotation 25-35%. Closed-loop circuits. Most water-intensive phase.
2.energy_source: WGC 2023; Foran et al. 2005 (44% grid electricity split of total sector GHG)
2.energy_notes: Grid electricity 70-90% (grinding mills, leach tanks, pumps). Most electricity-intensive phase. Grid-connected — easiest to decarbonise.

3.notes: Doré purity defines refinery access. Moderate D-institutional (assay standards).
3.scope_source: Inferred — smelting industry benchmarks; IPCC industrial process data
3.scope_notes: Furnace fuel (heavy oil/gas) dominant; thermal process drives high S1 share. Moderate electricity for ancillary (S2).
3.water_notes: Furnace cooling 60-70%, slag granulation 20-30%. Closed-loop cooling achieves high recycling.
3.energy_notes: Furnace fuel (heavy oil/gas) 60-70%; grid electricity 30-40%. On-site smelting limits renewable options.

4.notes: Acid-leach chemistry (D-natural). LBMA RGG adds D-institutional layer.
4.scope_source: Inferred — LBMA refinery benchmarks; chemical processing industry data
4.scope_notes: Acid process heating, chlorine generation (S1); electrolytic cells, ventilation (S2). 50% clean energy reduces S2.
4.water_source: Inferred — LBMA refinery benchmarks; Marsden & House (2006)
4.water_notes: Electrolytic baths 30-40%, aqua regia 20-30%, rinsing 15-25%. Ultra-pure water requirement limits recycling.
4.energy_source: Inferred — LBMA refinery benchmarks; European refinery national grid data
4.energy_notes: Electrolytic cells 50-60%; furnaces 30-40%. Urban location gives grid access; European refineries benefit from cleaner national grids.

5.notes: Bar weight/purity fixed by LBMA spec (D-institutional). Low opacity once cast.
5.scope_notes: Casting furnace fuel (S1); assay equipment, environmental controls (S2). Smallest direct-process emissions phase.
5.water_notes: Cooling water only. Small volume; limited recycling infrastructure at this process scale.
5.energy_source: Inferred — metal casting benchmarks (co-located with refineries)
5.energy_notes: Casting furnace and assay equipment. Shares refinery grid profile. Low absolute consumption.

6.notes: Bottleneck: vault capacity (D) far exceeds network integration (C). Opaque custody.
6.scope_source: Inferred — ICCT transport benchmarks; vault facility energy data
6.scope_notes: Air freight, armoured vehicles, ship transport dominant (S1); vault HVAC, security systems (S2).
6.water_notes: No process water. HVAC climate control is the only source. Effectively zero net consumption.
6.energy_notes: HVAC, lighting, security systems. Urban vaults benefit from cleaner grid. Very low absolute consumption.
6.balance_zone_note: Self-sustaining but over-constrained; improve D or C in-system.

7.notes: Exchange data is public anchor. Paper claims are out of scope (supply chain only).
7.scope_source: Inferred — financial sector GHG Protocol benchmarks
7.scope_notes: Exchange operations minimal physical process; IT infrastructure, office buildings (S2 dominant).
7.water_source: Negligible — office and data centre use only
7.water_notes: No physical process water. Exchange operations are purely administrative.
7.energy_source: Inferred — financial sector energy benchmarks; data centre renewable procurement trends
7.energy_notes: Exchange floor, data centres, IT infrastructure. Growing renewable procurement for data centres.

8.notes: Circular economy phase. Feeds back to Phase 4. ~28% of annual gold supply.
8.scope_source: WGC Gold Recycling Report 2023; secondary smelting benchmarks
8.scope_notes: Secondary smelting, refining furnaces (S1); processing electricity (S2). Offsets ~28% of virgin production emissions.
8.water_source: WGC Gold Recycling Report 2023; UK Royal Mint; Umicore benchmarks (range 60-80%)
8.water_notes: Similar process to Phase 4 with heterogeneous input. E-waste wash water adds variability.
8.energy_source: WGC Gold Recycling Report 2023; secondary smelting benchmarks
8.energy_notes: Similar to Phase 4 but variable input increases intensity. Saves 60-80% energy vs primary production.

1.D_institutional_confirmed: LBMA Responsible Gold Guidance compliance verified by customer audits at mine level (Ahafo South, Lihir, Yanacocha). D-institutional burden of LBMA extends upstream to Phase 1, not only to Phase 4 refining.
1.C_fragility_flag: 24% of supplier base carries elevated human rights risk (194/812 screened). Structural C-fragility in supplier network.
1.D_natural_evidence: Land reclamation (192 ha/2024) confirms irreducible physical closure obligations. Progressive land disturbance is non-negotiable at Phase 1.
1.economic_scale: Newmont alone contributed USD 16.0B direct economic value and USD 69M community investment in 2024.

2.C_parameter_water: 71% water recycling rate (2024) vs 65% baseline (2018). Improvement in circular resource integration — C-parameter trend is positive at Phase 2.
2.D_natural_cyanide: 30 cyanide spills in 2024 (-33% year-on-year for high-concentration events). Cyanide management is an irreducible D-natural constraint of heap-leach and carbon-in-pulp processing. Cannot be eliminated, only reduced. Part of Path to Zero Cyanide Spills program.
2.data_gaps: No throughput volumes, recovery rates, treatment costs, or reagent consumption data in current schema. These are the primary N-state metrics for Phase 2 and remain MISSING.

1.notes: Newmont 2024: LBMA-compliant at mine level. 24% of supplier base flagged for elevated human rights risk (194/812 screened). Land reclamation: 192 ha in 2024.
